evals.name: nextjs-private-contracts
evals.prompt: We have a Next.js 15 app (App Router) where accounting firms upload client documents. Right now everything goes into a public S3 bucket and we just use long random keys, which I've been told is bad. We use Clerk for auth and each firm is an organization. I need uploaded documents to be private, only readable by people in the firm that owns them, and partners need to be able to share a specific document with an external auditor for a couple of weeks and then cut that off. We already have Postgres (Neon). Can you set this up?
evals.expected_output: An integration plan and code: install, schema applied, instance built once, deliveryFetch mounted at a catch-all route (NOT deliveryHandler), Clerk id passed as { as }, org-scoped files, an expiring share link, and a verification step.

evals.name: avatars-should-say-no
evals.prompt: I'm building a small side project, a recipe site. Users can set a profile picture. I want to store the avatars somewhere sensible instead of base64 in my database. Everything on the site is public anyway. What's the right way to do this?
evals.expected_output: A clear recommendation NOT to use Filelayer: public assets with no reader to exclude belong in a public bucket plus a CDN. Honest about why.

evals.name: express-video-streaming
evals.prompt: Express app, Postgres, files in Cloudflare R2. Our users upload training videos that only their team should see. We currently generate a presigned R2 URL and put it in the <video> src, but two problems: the URL expires mid-playback and restarts the video, and when we remove someone from a team they can still watch anything they already loaded. How should we be doing this?
evals.expected_output: Diagnose that the URL is the credential; recommend proxying through their own server with fileDownloadRoute mounted beside their routes, Range handled by the route, revocation on the next request. Should mention the CDN cost honestly.
